decisions.reason: The black-finish range sits close to the core offer and fits the firm's design-led positioning, so it costs little to keep, and dropping a visible design line launched only a year ago would undercut that stated direction.

The firm built a dedicated page for this seamless-covering shower channel and it serves the barrier-free bathroom direction it has announced, so investment and public commitment both favour keeping it.

Pump-assisted drainage required extra development beyond the core offer and extends the firm's reach into renovation, so after only one year any weak uptake would still be read as a temporary start-up effect.
The tileable floor drain has its own page and sits close to the established offer, so management is committed to it and keeping it costs little.
The stainless steel design grate has its own page and draws on the firm's own manufacturing and design identity, so dropping it would contradict its public positioning.
